## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

content.text:
We need to build the game. No package.json — plain HTML/CSS/JS static. Three.js can be loaded from CDN? Better to vendor three.js locally to avoid network issues (though network probably available). Check if npm access. We can use CDN importmap (unpkg/jsdelivr) but preview may have network. Safer: check cached node modules or download three.js to vendor.

Let me plan the game design.

Concept: "Bieber Fever: Rock the Stage" — 3D rhythm game, horizontal lanes (played horizontally: fret highway moves right-to-left or left-to-right horizontally across screen), instruments guitar, bass, drums. Keys colored differently. Guitar Hero-like with Justin Bieber songs. 3D scene: stage with character silhouettes, note highway angled in perspective, notes sliding down/along track. Play horizontally means the note track travels horizontally (left to right) rather than vertically — spec says "played horizontally". So a horizontal note highway: a 3D runway extending to the right, notes approaching from the right toward a strike line on the left, each lane stacked vertically-ish? We can design note highway as horizontal scrolling: lanes are horizontal rows (like a sideways guitar hero), notes move right-to-left toward a vertical judgement line on left.

Keys for creating songs having different colors: keys mapped to note lanes, each with distinct color (D F J K style? For 3 instruments maybe). We can use 4 lanes per instrument, keys 1-4 guitar, Q-R? Let's design keyboard: For guitar: keys 1 2 3 4 with colors green/red/yellow/blue (Guitar Hero-ish). Bass: Q W E R with purple/orange/cyan/pink. Drums: A S D F with different colors. Actually playing one instrument at a time, switching instruments with Tab. Or all three at once? "The game should include More than one instrument, specifically guitar, bass, and drums." Could offer instrument selection in menu and track lanes for the chosen instrument; plus a "band" mode? Better: song has three instrument charts; player picks instrument. In-game, press Tab to switch? That would complicate. Simpler and more impressive: Play all three simultaneously in "Band mode": each instrument has its own 4-lane horizontal highway stacked vertically on left half, keys groups. But too hard. 

Alternative design: Each song section assigned to instruments; press instrument switch keys to play whichever lane incoming. Hmm.

Better UX: Menu choose instrument (Guitar/Bass/Drums) with different note colors and key mappings. Also allow "Band" mode where 3 horizontal highways stacked (guitar top, bass middle, drums bottom), keys 1-4 / Q-R / A-F, with drums requiring space? For drums, keyboard hits. That's a complete game. Default Guitar.

3D: Use Three.js for stage with animated crowd, spotlights, silhouettes, singer. Notes as glowing 3D blocks/rings moving along a perspective highway that stretches horizontally to the right. Since played horizontally, the note highway camera is angled so lanes go left-right, judgement line at left near camera, notes spawn at right/far. Hmm perspective.

Alternative interpretation: Screen is landscape, note lanes scroll horizontally across the bottom in 2D overlay while 3D stage above. But request "3D game ... played horizontally". I'll do real 3D perspective: camera looking down at a horizontal runway. Lanes run left-to-right; the strike line near the left; notes spawn far right and travel left. Camera positioned above and slightly behind strike line, looking rightward. Each lane offset along Z (depth on screen? no). Let's set world: X axis is scrolling direction (notes move -X), lanes spread along Z, highway plane y=0. Camera at (-8, 6, 0) looking toward +X with slight downward, so highway stretches into screen to the right. Four lanes along Z; perspective makes far end narrower. Judgement line at x=0. Notes appear from x=+18 and move toward 0. Hit effects.

Stage behind the highway? We can put stage on left side with performer and crowd in background. Camera view: highway in foreground right; stage visible left. A horizontal composition.

Maybe better camera: Highway is long X direction; camera at (6, 8, 14) looking at (6,0,0) so lanes spread horizontally across screen Z? Hmm, we want notes approach from right side of screen toward left. If X is world horizontal across screen, camera should look down from front with X mapping to screen x. Camera at (5, 9, 16) looking at (5,0,0): then +X appears right (roughly), -X left. Lanes spread along Z (depth), which maps to screen vertical-ish (foreshortened). Highway appears as a band going across screen. Notes spawn at right edge with lanes stacked vertically due to perspective. Camera could be rotated: camera positioned above, looking straight down but with perspective, X horizontal, Z vertical with far lanes smaller. That reads as horizontal lanes and works.

Let's set camera at (0, 14, 12) looking at (0,0,0) — typical; +X right, -Z far up-screen. Then highway crossing horizontally, lanes along Z stacked vertically. Notes travel from +X to -X. Strike line at world x = -2. Camera orbits subtly. Stage behind at -Z (top of screen) with performers, crowd. Actually the highway would occlude the stage. We can make highway semi-transparent floating grid over lower half and stage behind top. Fine.

Design a neon pop stage: singer (stylized Justin Bieber-ish silhouette, avoid copyrighted assets—use stylized figure with cap? Make character named "JB" maybe. User explicitly wants Justin Bieber. We can reference "Bieber Fever" and songs "Baby", "Sorry", "Peaches", "Love Yourself", "What Do You Mean?" — song titles are fine; we'll generate original chiptune/pop loops procedurally, no copyrighted audio. Note this assumption. 3D singer character with white shirt, cap, mic. Use simple geometry: capsule body, sphere head, hair, microphone. Backup dancers, crowd of low-poly heads bouncing, spotlights, speaker stacks, LED wall visualizer.

Audio: procedural WebAudio pop backing tracks per song (synth chords, bass, drums). Different BPM/keys. Hit sounds. Must handle iOS audio unlock via user gesture. Timing: use AudioContext.currentTime as clock for notes; requestAnimationFrame.

Charts: generate deterministic note charts per song/instrument from patterns synced to beats. For each instrument, 4 lanes. Drums maybe 4 pads with colored keys: A S D F (red, yellow, blue, green) or keys? "keys for creating songs having different colors" — unclear, could mean the keys used to create songs/play notes have different colors. We'll make every lane keycap color distinct and displayed in the HUD with glowing keycaps. Also include a "Studio" mode? Hmm "keys for creating songs" maybe means keys for playing the notes. We'll satisfy with color-coded keycaps mapped to lanes.

Could add a Song Creator mode where players compose a short loop using colored keys and play it back? The request: "with the keys for creating songs having different colors" likely translated: "with the keys for creating notes having different colors" = note keys have different colors. In Guitar Hero the 5 fret keys have colors. So lane colors distinct.

Scoring: Perfect/Great/Good/Miss, combo multiplier, star power "Bieber Fever" meter, hit accuracy, score, streak. Duration ~60-90 sec per song. Pause, restart, results. Countdown 3-2-1.

Menu: 3D stage as background, title, song cards (3 songs), instrument selector (Guitar/Bass/Drums), difficulty (Chill/Heartthrob/Superstar), controls legend, start button. Keyboard navigation and click/touch.

Mobile: responsive, touch controls: on-screen colored pads at bottom during horizontal play; 4 buttons per instrument. The highway horizontal. Safe areas. No motion needed.

Implementation approach: plain HTML with importmap to local three module. Download three.js from CDN to vendor using curl. Check network.
